# @kernelui-lib/elements — LLM reference

The same design as `@kernelui-lib/react`, shipped as framework-free Custom
Elements — light DOM (no shadow root, so the page's own Kernel stylesheet
reaches every component with no per-instance style duplication), zero
runtime dependencies. Use this package in Vue, Svelte, Astro, or plain
HTML; use `@kernelui-lib/react` instead in a React app.

## Install

```bash
npm install @kernelui-lib/elements @kernelui-lib/styles
```

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="path/to/@kernelui-lib/styles/index.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="path/to/@kernelui-lib/elements/dist/kernel.css" />
<script type="module">
  import "@kernelui-lib/elements"; // registers every <kernel-*> tag below
</script>

<kernel-button variant="primary">Save changes</kernel-button>
```

Importing the module registers every custom element via
`customElements.define` — there is no per-component import path, and no
separate "install this one component" step.

### Overriding Kernel's CSS

Load `@kernelui-lib/elements/styles.layer.css` (`dist/kernel.layer.css`)
instead of `styles.css` and any unlayered CSS you write overrides Kernel
without specificity fights or `!important`. It is the same CSS inside
`@layer kernel.components`, ordered after `@kernelui-lib/styles`'
`kernel.tokens` and `kernel.base` layers. Opt-in, because an unlayered
reset in your own CSS (`button { background: none }`) would also win; put
such a reset in a layer declared before Kernel's:
`@layer reset, kernel.tokens, kernel.base, kernel.components;` above your
imports.

### Editor and TypeScript support

- `dist/custom-elements.json`: a Custom Elements Manifest (schema 2.1.0),
  also named by `package.json`'s `customElements` field and exported as
  `@kernelui-lib/elements/custom-elements.json`. Every tag with its class,
  description, observed attributes and events.
- `dist/vscode.html-custom-data.json`: VS Code HTML custom data. Add its
  path to `html.customData` in `.vscode/settings.json` for completion in
  `.html` files.
- `@kernelui-lib/elements/jsx` (`dist/jsx.d.ts`): declares every tag in
  React 19's `JSX.IntrinsicElements`. Load it with
  `import type {} from "@kernelui-lib/elements/jsx";` (or list it in
  `compilerOptions.types`). Attributes take a string, number or boolean;
  events are `on<eventname>` props with the exact event name, React 19's
  custom element syntax: `<kernel-tabs onvaluechange={(e) => e.detail.value}>`.

## Conventions (mirrors @kernelui-lib/react's prop conventions as attributes)

- **Value**: a `value` attribute (or a `values`/`tags`-style JS property
  where a value can't serialize into a plain string, e.g. `TagInput`'s
  `.tags`), and a `change` event — `event.detail` carries the parsed
  value where a `change` event's default (the raw element) isn't enough
  (e.g. `<kernel-tag-input>` dispatches `{ detail: { tags: string[] } }`).
- **Form-field scaffold**: `label` (required — still the input's
  accessible name even when `hide-label` is set), `hide-label` (boolean
  attribute), `description`, `error-message`, `invalid`, `disabled`,
  `required` — same names as `@kernelui-lib/react`'s form fields, kebab-case.
- **Boolean attributes are presence-based**: `<kernel-checkbox disabled>`
  means disabled; there is no `disabled="false"` — omit the attribute
  entirely to mean false. (Exception, clearly named to avoid the
  ambiguity: `<kernel-color-picker no-hex-input>`, an opt-out boolean,
  since the React version's equivalent prop defaults to `true`.)
- **Real elements, real events**: every component wraps a genuine native
  element or ARIA pattern internally and re-dispatches its real DOM
  events (`input`, `change`, `click`) — listen for those directly, no
  proprietary event system. `<kernel-file-upload>` additionally
  dispatches `kernel-file-upload-error` with
  `detail: { type: "accept" | "max-size" | "max-files" | "directory", files }`
  when a pick or drop is rejected.
- **Contrast**: Kernel's colour tokens are checked with APCA (the
  perceptual method proposed for WCAG 3), with WCAG 2's ratio as a floor:
  - `--kernel-color-text`: Lc 75 and 4.5:1;
  - `--kernel-color-text-muted`: Lc 60 and 4.5:1;
  - `--kernel-color-focus-ring` and `--kernel-color-border-control`: Lc 45
    and 3:1.

  Keep to those tokens for text and outlines. If you set your own colours,
  check them against the same APCA levels, not just WCAG 2. Dark mode is
  where the two methods disagree most.
- **Compose with real children**: components that take structured content
  use real child elements or attributes on real children, not a JSON
  prop — e.g. `<kernel-select>` takes real `<option>`/`<optgroup>`
  children, `<kernel-tabs>` takes `<kernel-tab>`/`<kernel-tab-panel>`.
- **Icons in pills** (`<kernel-badge>`, `<kernel-tag-input>`'s tags,
  `<kernel-suggestion-item>`, `<kernel-button>`): put any `<svg>` or `<img>` child before the
  text, after it, or on its own. Mark any other icon element (an icon
  custom element, say) with `data-icon`. Whichever end holds an icon
  becomes a `1lh` slot, concentric with the rounded end, and stays correct
  if the children change later. Tune the whole set with
  `--kernel-icon-size` and `--kernel-icon-stroke-width`. Label an
  icon-only pill on the icon itself (`role="img" aria-label="…"`), or an
  icon-only `<kernel-button>` with `aria-label` on the tag.
- **Built-in strings go through labels**: every piece of English a tag
  renders on its own is overridable with a `label-<key>` attribute (the
  React `labels` key in kebab-case): `<kernel-dialog label-close="Fermer">`,
  `<kernel-date-picker label-previous-month="Mois précédent"
  label-weekdays="di,lu,ma,me,je,ve,sa">`. Interpolated strings are
  `{name}` templates: `label-remove-tag="Supprimer {tag}"`. Or set the
  `labels` property with the same keys as React's `<Name>Labels` (values
  may be functions): `el.labels = { removeTag: (tag) => … }`; the property
  wins over the attribute. Unset keys keep their English default.

## Agent skills and MCP

This package ships agent skills in `skills/` (`kernel-ui-elements`), versioned with the code. `npx @kernelui-lib/cli agents` installs them, registers the `kernel` MCP server (exact props, tokens, `check_code`), and adds a Kernel section to AGENTS.md.

## Tags (grouped to match @kernelui-lib/react's component groups; composite
## components' sub-tags are one level deeper, e.g. <kernel-card-header>
## goes inside <kernel-card>)

- Primitives: `kernel-avatar`, `kernel-badge`, `kernel-button`, `kernel-checkbox`, `kernel-kbd`, `kernel-label`, `kernel-radio-group` (+ `kernel-radio-group-item`), `kernel-separator`, `kernel-switch`, `kernel-toggle`

- Layout: `kernel-card` (+ `kernel-card-header`/`kernel-card-title`/`kernel-card-description`/`kernel-card-content`/`kernel-card-footer`), `kernel-footer`, `kernel-header`, `kernel-nav` (+ `kernel-nav-link`), `kernel-resizable`, `kernel-scroll-area`, `kernel-sidebar`
- Feedback: `kernel-callout`, `kernel-empty-state`, `kernel-progress`, `kernel-skeleton`, `kernel-toast-viewport`
- Overlays: `kernel-command-palette`, `kernel-context-menu`, `kernel-dialog`, `kernel-dropdown-menu` (+ `kernel-dropdown-menu-morph`/`kernel-menu-item`/`kernel-menu-separator`), `kernel-hover-card`, `kernel-navigation-menu` (+ `kernel-nav-menu-item`/`kernel-nav-menu-link`/`kernel-nav-menu-trigger`/`kernel-nav-menu-content`), `kernel-popover`, `kernel-sheet`, `kernel-tooltip`
- Navigation: `kernel-breadcrumbs` (+ `kernel-breadcrumb-item`), `kernel-pagination` (+ `kernel-pagination-item`/`kernel-pagination-previous`/`kernel-pagination-next`/`kernel-pagination-ellipsis`), `kernel-tabs` (+ `kernel-tabs-list`/`kernel-tab`/`kernel-tab-panel`)
- Data Display: `kernel-accordion` (+ `kernel-accordion-item`), `kernel-carousel` (+ `kernel-carousel-slide`), `kernel-data-table`, `kernel-date-picker`, `kernel-date-range-picker`, `kernel-table` (+ `kernel-table-caption`/`kernel-table-header`/`kernel-table-body`/`kernel-table-row`/`kernel-table-head`/`kernel-table-cell`)
- AI: `kernel-agent-activity` (+ `kernel-agent-activity-item`), `kernel-attachment` (+ `kernel-attachment-list`), `kernel-code-block`, `kernel-composer`, `kernel-file-diff`, `kernel-message-list` (+ `kernel-message`/`kernel-message-bubble`), `kernel-message-scroller`, `kernel-model-picker`, `kernel-reasoning`, `kernel-sources` (+ `kernel-source`/`kernel-citation`), `kernel-streaming-markdown`, `kernel-suggestion` (+ `kernel-suggestion-item`), `kernel-thinking-indicator`, `kernel-todo-list` (+ `kernel-todo-item`), `kernel-tool-approval`, `kernel-tool-call`, `kernel-usage-meter`

## Utilities

- **`DetailsPanelAnimator`** — The measured-height open/close motion behind
  `<kernel-accordion-item>`, `<kernel-reasoning>` and `<kernel-tool-call>`,
  exported for building your own `<details>` disclosure with the same feel.
  Construct it with `new DetailsPanelAnimator(detailsEl, contentEl, { onOpenChange })`,
  where `contentEl` is a single wrapper holding everything except the
  `<summary>`; call `setOpen(boolean)` to drive it programmatically,
  `snapOpen(boolean)` to jump without animating, and `destroy()` to detach. It
  drives the panel from `click` on the `<summary>` rather than the `toggle`
  event, because `toggle` is non-cancelable and fires only *after* the browser
  has already painted the panel at full height. Honours
  `prefers-reduced-motion` by snapping, and sets `data-state="opening"` /
  `"closing"` on the `<details>` while in flight.
- **`KernelElement`**, **`kernelClass`**, **`dataAttr`** — The base class and
  class-name helpers the elements themselves use.

## Where to look for exact attributes

This file is a map, not the source of truth. `dist/custom-elements.json`
lists every tag's observed attributes and events in one file. Every
component class also has a JSDoc comment listing its attributes (search
`dist/index.d.ts` for the tag's class, e.g. `KernelTextField`, or read
the source under `src/components/<Name>/<Name>.ts`). If this package was
installed alongside the project's docs site, `/labs/elements` runs every
tag live with zero React on the page.
